utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The quotation I made was brief, so I hope they didn't have too much of a problem. But as I was saying, there was a temporary recognition of a state established on the basis of a decision which had no legitimacy whatsoever because it was not supported by all three peoples, and the decision represented a great threat to the fact that the Serb people in Bosnia-Herzegovina should become peoples of the second order within a Muslim fundamental state. You saw a moment ago what the Mujahedin looked like, how many thousands had gathered there in that place, in that new battlefield which was open for the first time in Europe. And you were also -- you have also seen many other things that have been accessible to you, but I'll return to that in due course. During the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina, in Serbia and Montenegro but predominantly, of course, in Serbia, from the wartime clashes several thousand citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina took refuge amongst whom there were several tens of thousands who were Muslims. Now, if it were true that Serbia were the aggressor, then so many thousands of Bosnian Muslims would never have got the idea of taking refuge in Serbia proper. Even some Muslim military units, when they were facing the Serbian army, crossed the Drina River to find salvation in Serbia itself. And Serbia did not send them back but it behaved in a very humane manner towards them; it fed them, it clothed them, it looked after them and then enabled them, via the International Red Cross, to go to other third countries. On one such occasion when I approved a whole Muslim brigade, numbering 850 people, to go across the Drina River and find salvation in Serbia, I wrote a letter to Izetbegovic. I'm not going to read out the whole of that letter but just a small passage from it in which I said: "Your soldiers were not greeted here as enemies, as foes, but as human beings, as neighbours who, through force of circumstance, had entered the flames of war against their will. You know full well that we offered them hospitality in Yugoslavia, to hundreds of thousands of refugees and tens of thousands are your own compatriots. And all of them have the same treatment and our care is afforded to them. More courage is necessary to conclude peace than to start a war. I entreat you to make such a decision in the interests of your own peoples and the people living on the territory of the former Yugoslavia. Just as I would like to ask General Ratko Mladic and the leadership of Republika Srpska to cease the war and to cease hostilities with the representatives of your army." That's the kind of letter that I sent to General Mladic as well. The Serbs in Croatia - let us go back to that broader area; the Serbs in Bosnia, in Republika Srpska, in Krajina, Serbs in Serbia and Serbs in Yugoslavia - not in a single phase of the Yugoslav crisis brought into question or challenged the right of the Croatian people or the Muslim people or any other people, constituent people of Yugoslavia, to their right to self-determination. And this undoubtedly includes the right to secession. The war in Croatia and Bosnia, therefore, had no sense nor did it have any reason in furthering this right to self-determination and the secession of the Croatian people because nobody challenged that right at all. Its sense and meaning was in the crimes perpetrated over the Serbs, in expelling 600.000 Serbs -- Carrington mentions that figure himself so I don't want to change it. So at least 600.000 Serbs from their territories in the then-administrative, non-state borders of the Republic of Croatia. And in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the meaning and sense of the war was in expelling the Serb people and making them second-rate citizens within Bosnia-Herzegovina, which was conceived as a future Islamic republic. In addition to the quotation that, as far as I was able to see wasn't properly interpreted, it was too fast and I don't mind that, on Banja Latic Terriga [phoen] in 1992 what was said was, and I quote: "There would have been no war had Croatia not wished for war." But we assess that it was only through war that we could achieve the independence of Croatia. That is why we waived a policy of negotiation, and behind those negotiations, we set up our armed units. Had we not done so, we would not have reached our goal. And Stjepan Mesic, whom you saw on your screens on television a moment ago for a very brief period, says in the Croatian Sabor, or parliament, and he was the then-president of the Presidency of Yugoslavia, on the 5th of December, 1991, stated the following, his famous line: "I think I have fulfilled my task; Yugoslavia exists no more." Now, if to that you add the well-known fact of the Islamic declaration by Alija Izetbegovic in which he says that among -- between the Muslim religion and non-Muslim states and institutions there can never be peace between the two nor can there be co-existence, and you were able to see them calling for a holy war, the jihad and all the rest of it, then I think that everybody -- you -- who needn't even be well-intentioned but if they are honest must be quite clear on what it was all about. So it was not the Serb who brought into question the right of any constituent peoples to their self-determination. All we considered then and we consider today is that the right of self-determination also belongs to the Serbian people and that everything that was taken away from them by force, by violation of that right does not hold water in terms of international law and legality and cannot be recognised under any pressure whatsoever. As for this false indictment, it deprives the Serbs of all human rights, including the right to life, the right to self-defence, because in Croatia and in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Serbs defended the areas where they had been living for centuries. Charles Boyd, who we saw in another statement awhile ago, the Deputy Head of the US forces in Europe, he wrote in Foreign Affairs September/October 1995, I'm quoting: [In English] "The popular image of this war is one of unrelenting Serb expansion. Much of what the Croatians called the 'occupied territories' is land that has been held by Serbs for more than three centuries. The same is true of most Serb land in Bosnia where the Western media frequently refer to as the 70 per cent of Bosnia size by rebel Serbs. In short, the Serbs were not trying to conquer new territory but merely to hold onto what was already theirs." [Interpretation] Now the 23rd of July, 1993, the co-chairman of the International Conference on the former Yugoslavia, Lord Owen, when rejecting the possibility of a military intervention in Bosnia-Herzegovina, which is what Clinton's hawks and paid lobbies insisted upon all the time, that rejection of military intervention is something that he explained in the following words, I quote: "It is very difficult to intervene in a situation which is not aggression." And he adds: "That was always a conflict between the Serbs in Bosnia, the Muslims in Bosnia, and the Croats in Bosnia." And the former US Secretary of State Henry Kissinger, in his article in the Washington Post on the 17th of May, 1993, says, inter alia, again I'm quoting, that: "In Bosnia-Herzegovina, there is a civil war going on, that there is not a Bosnian ethnic group, and that the international community made a big mistake by recognising that republic." He says that this is a three-fold civil war, not an invasion of a neighbouring state against a sovereign state. Croatia and Serbia support their compatriots in Bosnia. The most irresponsible mistake in the current Bosnian tragedy was the international recognition of the Bosnian state under the authority of the Muslims. There is the precedent of the premature recognition of Slovenia and Croatia by Germany and in this way the international community created all the new-founded states in the territory of the former Yugoslavia and so on. So I quoted two Americans and one Brit, and not to say an Englishman because David Owen is Welsh, but there are many others, other Americans, Britons, Russians, Frenchmen, Russians, Indians, Germans, Italians who publicly stated what the true state of affairs was. Many will have the opportunity of personally testifying here, as opposed to the practice of false witnesses and secret witnesses that the other side has. I quoted only these three persons in order to make my assertion undisputed; that the truth about the civil war had to be well known to those who were the actual decision-makers. However, the resounding cannonades of the media war made it impossible for the truth to come through. You saw on these films part of it, and I would like to show that this was a very well-organised and very well-paid, well-financed propaganda. Since I do not have time, I'm going to illustrate this by one example, linking it precisely to what you saw in the film concerning the engagement of Rudder and Finn. A special role in demonising the Serbs was played precisely by that company in different periods. A paid -- there was a paid representative of Muslims and Croats in Bosnia. James Hart, the director of Rudder Finn boasted by these sensational reports that led to a dramatic increase in the support of US intervention in Bosnia-Herzegovina, as he said to a French journalist Jacques Merlinot in April 1993, he was proud of how his firm manipulated the Jewish public opinion. This was a major success because the Croatian President Tudjman was, as he said, very careless in his book 'The Horrors of War', and he could have been accused of anti-Semitism for that. And the Bosnian President Izetbegovic also had serious problems with his image because his book 'The Islamic Declaration' shows that there is far too great support to an Islamist fundamentalist state. Even more so as the past of Croatia and Bosnia is indeed marked by cruel anti-Semitism and that is what Hart admits and speaks of the tens of thousands of Jews who went missing in Nazi camps. And that was a reason why Jewish organisations and individuals should not have much patience for the Croats and Muslims in Bosnia. And he said: "For us it was a challenge to totally reverse such a position, and we did this masterfully." How masterfully they succeeded. You see, if-- Roy Gutman wrote stories in Newsday about the alleged Serb death camps - he indeed won a Pulitzer Prize for this - but it was eventually established that all of this was a lie. And then Hart's people were in a position to mobilise some of the main Jewish organisations, the American Jewish Committee, B'nai B'rith, the Anti-Libel League, and the US Congress. And he says that this was an incredible success when the Jewish organisations came into the game on the side of the Bosnians. Then we could immediately, he says, turn the Serbs into villains in the entire game. And when Merlinot asked him, "Well, you did this but you didn't have any proof for it, didn't you? You did not know whether this was true." And he answered him -- because he said, "Actually, everything you had was just this Newsday article." And his answer was, "Our job is not to check out information. We had a job to do and we did it. We are not paid to moralise." However, it is quite clear that Rudder Finn was not that successful because, as they had put it, masterfully carried through all these promotion tricks. What made the efforts of this firm effective is the receptiveness of the Western media. They were going along with the suggestions of those who were making political moves in Washington, Bonn, the Vatican, and they themselves were creating an anti-Serb atmosphere many months before the Rudder Finn campaign. However, Jewish organisations did not accept this story because they were simply gullible and only because of this masterfully executed job by Rudder Finn; this was also due to the interest they had. They wanted to repel the fury of the Arab states, the Muslim states to anyone, and in this case it was deflected to the Serbs. And that is how they repaid the Serbs for the protection of Jews in the Second World War, in which in the occupied territories of the Balkans it was only Serbs in Serbia who, at the cost of their own lives, managed to protect them from pogroms. And they themselves know that. They are ashamed of that, at least those who talked to me. And I hope that some of them are going to testify about this here. Precisely because of this enormous help given to the Jews and also this brotherhood between peoples, not states. That was between the Serb people and the Jewish people. utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this practically monopolistic communications stream was assisted by some well-paid humanitarian groups, such as Doctors Without Borders; peaceful groups, Women Wearing Black, Human Rights Watch, the Human Rights Committee, along with other organisations. You saw in this film George Kenney, who was in charge of the Yugoslav desk at the State Department. He says the genocide indictment was repeated so many times in relation to Bosnia that proof became irrelevant. The American administration, he says, has no proof of any genocide, and anybody who reads the newspapers can see that there is a lack of evidence regardless of endless speculations. That is blood chilling. Another person who writes about this very extensively in his book To Kill the Nation, is Michael Parenth [phoen], and I gave you this book a couple of months ago. I don't know if you paid any attention to it, but it does contain a great deal of information. However, in order to illustrate how history is falsified and how lies are promoted, I'm going to show you yet another tape, a very short one, only a few minutes, so that you can see how this was done and what the effects were. Could you please have the tape played. In the meantime, I'm going to explain to you -- you're going to see at the very beginning that on the compact disk, 'The Chronology of the Twentieth Century', when you open the year 1992, then on it, at the very beginning, the symbol for the year 1992 is this forged story about the so-called death camps in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Please play the tape now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the CD I mentioned, 'The Chronicle of the 20th Century'. Now, when you look at the various years, 1992, you click 1992 and here's the image. It is this fabrication that entered history. You open it and this is what you see; about concentration camps.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: "SPEAKER: Here is Thomas Deichmann [phoen]. He was the German journalist who first raised suspicions about these famous ITN pictures. He is saying, Look at some newspapers. Most of the Western media. Not only is there no real difference in opinion on foreign policy matters, but even the same phrases are repeated. You see the same pictures with the same captions again and again. The ITN pictures bothered Deichmann. Looking at them one night, his wife noticed something: ITN claimed the Bosnian Muslims were imprisoned behind barbed wire. Why, she wondered, was the wire attached on their side of the fence? They could pull out the nails. Deichmann smelled a rat. He suspected the photos had been fabricated. He suspected special camera angles, tricky editing. He wanted to go to Trnopolje to see for himself, and there he saw the concentration camp that never existed. "Examining things on location, Deichmann saw what had been done. The reporters, Penny Marshall and the others in her crew, were in a barbed-wire enclosed space near a transformer station and barn. From there, they took pictures of refugees who were walking around quite freely outside the fence. During this visit, Deichmann made a drawing of the buildings and people as they appeared on the day the ITN crew filmed at Trnopolje. There was a barn and a transformer station, a refugee centre building, an open-air reception area, a recreation area near the refugee centre, the fenced-in area from inside which the ITN crew did their filming, and the barbed wire and chicken wire which was portrayed as evidence of a death camp at Trnopolje. "After the conversation with the Red Cross representative, we passed a group of new refugees. They were being registered by the civil authorities. Ms. Marshall chose not to set up her cameras and film in this open area. Instead, she and her crew manoeuvred into a partly-enclosed space used as a storage area for wheelbarrows and the like. The dilapidated fence had chicken wire on the bottom and a few strands of barbed wire on top to discourage theft. Our crew filmed the ITN people as they manoeuvred into this area through a hole in the broken down fence, then we followed and both crews set up within the enclosure, filming the refugees wandering around outside. There were heaps of material in barrels and we kept stumbling over them while trying to set up. Ms. Penny Marshall tried to talk to the nearest refugees but in vain since she didn't speak Serbo-Croatian. People searched for someone who could speak English. Someone in front of the crowd of refugees said, Here, this one speaks English, pointing to go Mr. Mehmed in the overalls. Mr. Bozanic, from the Yugoslav crew, filmed Penny Marshall's conversation with Mehmed. Later, the following was shown on Yugoslav TV, with Mr. Bozanic supplying an informal translation of the English conversation. "'No, no. They're very nice,' says Mehmed. Mehmed adds -- "SPEAKER: Do you feel safe here? "SPEAKER: He feels very safe here and, except for the heat, everything was fine. "SPEAKER: This man is very thin, insisted the reporter, and Mehmed said. "SPEAKER: The people are not the same. "SPEAKER: ... cameras behind barbed wire. She was in position. Now she searched the crowd for that perfect look. She wanted a star for her story, the story she would sell the world. You will see her conversation with Mehmed from our camera's angle once again. To make it clearer this time, here is a little diagram showing the position of the two crews. The ITN people are the blue circle on the left. We are the red circle on the right. Because the film crews were a yard apart, we filmed the same shots from a slightly different angle. Sometimes we filmed the ITN people as well. Ms. Marshall is interviewing Mehmed. "SPEAKER: Hello. "SPEAKER: My name Mehmed. "SPEAKER: Now did you come to be here? "SPEAKER: I think it's very fine [inaudible]. It's very hot. "SPEAKER: Outside. "SPEAKER: No, no. Inside. "SPEAKER: [inaudible]. "SPEAKER: No, no, no. Inside. "SPEAKER: Why did you come here? Are you a fighter? Are you a fighter? "SPEAKER: No. No. "SPEAKER: They came to your house and took you. "SPEAKER: Yes, yes. "SPEAKER: Do you feel safe here? "SPEAKER: I think it is very safe but it's very hot. Other things, it's very -- "SPEAKER: This man is very thin. "SPEAKER: He is very thin, but I think that is -- [inaudible]. All the people is not the same. [inaudible] I think it's refugee camp [inaudible]. "SPEAKER: Where are the women and the children? "SPEAKER: The women and children [inaudible] "SPEAKER: Every day during school holidays. "SPEAKER: It's not a prison. It's refugee camp. "SPEAKER: Where do you want to go? "SPEAKER: Home. "SPEAKER: Do you still have a home? "SPEAKER: [inaudible] [indiscernible] "SPEAKER: Very thin one to the right. "SPEAKER: The raw material was all there. Back in her editing room, Marshall and her associates saw just how beautiful this raw material could be. Perfect for fabricating a death camp. Give me the lower mask, upper, right, left. So just as the terrible fighting in Bosnia had deprived these unhappy men of their homes, now Ms. Marshall's pictures, which circled the world, cost them their legs as well. "Allow us to demonstrate how Marshall doctored the pictures to make them suitable for use by newspapers and magazines. We'll illustrate by repeating the process. Stop on those two. Now, give me a still shot. Now give me the Nouvel Observateur underneath. Notice the difference in the camera angles. Remember, their crew was shooting more to the left, which is why our camera picked up three men, where their camera picked up two. "Let's go back to the live picture, do the doctoring the way they have done it. Go to the guy in the blue shirt. Stop. Give me the right mask, please. Blow it up. Now add the fellow on the right, the one in black and white. Now kill the colour on the blonde one. Now fade out. That's it. Fade out with the short zoom lens. Move our picture back and below give me the Nouvel Observateur picture. Blow up Nouvel Observateur. "Scan. Compare. Bingo. One Nazi nightmare. "Give me the live picture shot again, the shot where they push Fikret towards Penny. The right and left mask. Upper and lower. Blow it up. Now give us Humanitage image. Give me the live picture again. Upper and lower. The left and right mask. Blow it up. Give me the magazine Novo with Welt's picture. "The spin-doctors of this world still didn't trust their readers to get the message, so they made it perfectly clear. They added World War II Nazi concentration camp snapshots, complete with real barbed wire. "SPEAKER: In the US, Bill Clinton and George Bush competed over who was the most horrified by the revelations of Serbian so-called atrocities proven by the pictures taken at Trnopolje. Referring to these clips during the pre-election campaign in 1992, Bill Clinton demanded that George Bush immediately bomb the Serbs. Not to be outdone, during a TV speech, George Bush compared the refugee camps with Nazi death camps."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, again could you give us the source of this film?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Was that -- was that a Yugoslav film that we saw there?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are witnesses. Some of them are Yugoslavs, others are not. This man Deichmann, as you know, is the editor-in-chief of the magazine Novo, which was the first to doubt this and go there. You know that Paddy Ashdown spoke of those camps, but when he was invited by the authorities of Republika Srpska to visit the spot, he was unable to find any camps there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Do we take it that the compilation was made by you and your team?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. You may take it that this was prepared for me by my assistants, but these are facts, because there are innumerable witnesses who can prove that this was an open refugee centre where one could come and go freely. You also heard this man Mehmed saying that he felt very safe there and that the only thing that was bothering him was the August heat. I would like to remind you, however, that when I quoted those people - I'm referring to Kissinger, Owen - I did this in order to show that those who were pulling the strings knew very well what this was about. It was not about the truth but about interests. The civil war in Yugoslavia was started when the survival of Yugoslavia was evidently contrary to the strategic interests of the USA, the Catholic church, Germany, and others. That Vatican knew what consequences could be expected can be seen from the Papal letter of 1 May 1991 where he speaks of the collapse of communism and says that this could give rise to grievous conflicts and much sorrow. And he asks for international structures to consolidate in order to intervene and arbitrate in the conflicts arising among nations. After the breakout of the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1992, the Vatican asked for military arbitration by the West, and it is evidently what they meant. This is the Encyclo Sentissimo Anno [phoen], published in Milan in 1991. There is no dispute that Germany and the Vatican were the first to recognise Croatia as an independent state. All this, however, especially the military intervention against the Serbian people in Republika Srpska, could not have taken place without the leading role of America in the form of Clinton's administration which will go down in history because of the crimes that took place on the European continent after World War II against German -- against the allies they had had in both wars, for American policy, Islamic extremism was given precedence, especially because of their role in destabilising the former Soviet Central Asia where there are large reserves of oil. And also because Islamic extremism, unconventional weapons for destroying the future of Russia and partly China, and it is well known that Chinese leaders spoke of the green transversal from China to the Adriatic Sea, and that is because the easiest and cheapest way to break down the anti-Islamic American extremism is because Serbian interests could be neglected. They didn't count. After the 11th of September, I am no longer sure that even American lives were taken seriously by Clinton. I cannot say precisely how many of those thousands of Mujahedins reviewed by Izetbegovic, as we saw on the tape, took part later in the terrorist activities against America, but I can say that under Clinton, America allowed Iran and Saudi Arabia to arm these murderers. Clinton's policy opened up a new European war theatre for Islamic fundamentalism. It was the forerunner of the next step, which was the 11th of September. I have here - I do not want to waste time by giving it to you now but I will tender it - a source which is not Serbian but Croatian; from the gaol in Busovaca, a list of Mujahedin who are in prison, taken prisoner by the Croatian army, coming from Algiers, Tunisia, Pakistan, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Turkey, and so on and so forth. Military ID cards, photo copies of these. One of these was a general. His name was Ganed Gamal, from Egypt. From a Special Purpose Unit of the Supreme Command, the Special Purpose Units were the ones who mainly perpetrated the crimes for which the Serbs were blamed later. However, I have no illusions that the Prosecutor will accuse Holbrooke and Clinton for the ethnic cleansing of thousands of Serbs from Croatia and mass murders or 550.000 Serbs from the Muslim Croatian federation, part of which is in Republika Srpska and part of whom are in Serbia, but I believe that the judiciary of the USA and its citizens cannot easily overlook the facts that show that they are the ones who opened up the door -- opened up the way to September 11th. And they will be called here to answer my questions and explain some facts. When speaking of this, I wish to point out that I'm speaking of Clinton's Administration because I believe that the previous Administration would not have perpetrated such a crime against the Serbs regardless of the strategic interest they had. They would not have gone so far, and they would have stuck to political means. I base this on the statement made by Secretary of State Baker before the American Congress in 1995, who said: "It is a fact that Slovenia and Croatia unilaterally declared independence in spite of our warnings. They used force to take the border crossings, and this led to civil war." He says that the position of the USA, the standpoint of the USA, that the territorial integrity of the -- of Yugoslavia should be preserved was supported by 32 states of the OSCE, and it is unfortunate that we did not adhere to that policy longer than we did. It was the Clinton administration that changed that policy. And we also heard Powell at the end of the film. But we also heard Holbrooke, who obviously tried to keep up with his boss and his statement about the Serbs being to blame for two world wars. There is no doubt that Holbrooke, as the American ambassador in Germany, played a key role in incorporating German standpoints into American policy. And as we heard on the film, there were eminent Americans and those who implemented Clinton's policy and the genocide over the Serbs. We saw his role in the attack on the Krajina and on the western part of Republika Srpska. For almost an entire decade, those who developed the strategy, the strategy called Belgrade Cradle of Evil, in Europe, not taking into account what was really happening in the Balkans but how it should be presented to public opinion. However, not everyone was obedient, and I think that history will not be altered here. They will not be successful in that, just as the NATO crimes on Kosovo were not successfully denied by Madam Del Ponte when she said that there was no basis for an investigation against NATO, because the key issue, the issue of human conscience and accepting falsehood as truth will always be present. The role of Germany in the collapse of Yugoslavia is well known, and that is why I will not go into detailed explanations. However, I would like to point out the special role of their interests as well as the role of the Catholic church and the role of Genscher's and Kinkel's party which was founded by Frederich Naumann who published a book in 1915 called 'Central Europe' as a project for organising a large part of the European continent around Germany as the centre. Later on, he published a book about Bulgaria and Central Europe in which he envisages a territorial contact after the victory in World War II. It was Naumann who said that the Serbs were a factor that was constantly upsetting the balance there. What they were really upsetting was the achievement of Imperialist goals at the expense of their own freedom. And the situation is the same today. Attempts are being made to falsify history, and this is what Holbrooke advocated. When we bear all this in mind, the expansion of Islamic fundamentalism, and I quote: "The bloody borders are to extend from Indonesia and Somalia to Bosnia." This is what Huntington wrote in his book 'The Clash of Civilisations and The Remaking of the World Order', published in New York in 1996. And when we look at this and compare it to Vatican and the Pope's project, the interests of Germany and, above all, America as the only superpower, it is evident that in the whole world there is no other example of a small nation being drawn into the interests of all the great powers. In spite of that, it was hard to destroy a big and respectable European country, one of the co-founders of the UN, as Yugoslavia was, and it proved to be impossible without the use of force and without a major crime. That is how the war was produced, the war of which all the Yugoslav peoples were the victims. And the Serbian people were victims on a global scale because they were declared to be guilty. That war had the same genocidal character just like the wars waged against Serbia during the Second World War by Ustashas and the rest, and Carrington knew this full well. In his interview to the Vienna journal Profile on the 1st of December, 1993, he said that he was being accused of being pro-Serbian, and he says that is simply nonsensical. It was not easy to say who was the good one and who was the bad one. When the Croats proclaimed their independence, they did not give the Serbs in their own country - and there are 600.000 of them - any guarantees whatsoever. It was therefore understandable that for this reason the Serbs were very worried. First of all, if we bear in mind the villainy of the Ustashas during World War II. And then he says again: "We almost had a solution to the Krajina and Slavonia problem. But at that particular point, the European Community at the end of 1991 decided to recognise Slovenia and Croatia. Croatia received what it wanted, Slovenia did too, and they no longer had the desire for the peace conference to be continued. And what is more important is that, for that same matter, we should enable the same for others. Bosnia-Herzegovina in the first place. But Izetbegovic opted for independence, although it was quite clear to him too that an option of that kind meant war. Hans Dietrich Genscher wanted international recognition for Slovenia and Croatia. Practically all the others were opposed to this." And the New York Times on the 14th of April, 1993, had this following brief news item: Interviewed in the United Nations building, Cyrus Vance said that what he called premature recognition of Slovenia and Herzegovina by the USA had led to the war, the war that was an ongoing one. Editor-in-chief of the New York Times, Rosenthal, in his leading article in December 1994 said that during the winter of 1991 and 1992, the Western countries, by their acts, brought woe to the Balkans. And this led to the fact that a civil war was imminent in Bosnia-Herzegovina where the Muslims were never a nation but just an administrative unit in Yugoslavia. And he goes on to say that the conflict in Yugoslavia was caused precisely by the premature recognition of Yugoslavia under the pressure of Croatia and that the independent Bosnian state was set up as a result. Lord Owen, on the 12th of November, 1995, in an interview to the Spanish daily El Paz, said, "I have great respect for the United States, but in recent years, the diplomacy of that particular country is responsible for the prolonged war in Bosnia. Had Washington supported the peace plan in 1993, a great number of dead would have been avoided. So this is not one opinion but it is the facts that I wish to point to," and that is the end of the quotation. I'm going to skip Cyrus Vance on other occasions, but I will just mention an explanation given by the one-time Greek Foreign Minister Saminos who was present at the meeting of the European Community on the 16th of December, 1991, and who on the 20th of November, 1992, at Elostiroskipous, [phoen] explained what was going on. The German Foreign Minister Genscher said, Saminos said on the 16th of December in the evening, that what was unavoidable was that if 11 of us vote for a united Yugoslavia that on the 15th of January, Germany in 1992 will certainly recognise Slovenia and Croatia as independent states. And that is in fact what came to pass. That's what happened. All the other international communities, the Americans later on accepted German policy, says Saminos. And the story goes on, as we know it. Maastricht and a unified European foreign policy, the great powers, the French and the English, had as Saminos said who took part in the meeting, representing Greece, had to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. accept the German blackmail. And Bulan Erdjevic [phoen], the former Turkish Premier said that Yugoslavia should have been preserved and that Turkey had to try to stop the disintegration of that particular federation in the Balkans. Erdjevic blamed Germany and Austria in part for the disintegration of Yugoslavia. "Yugoslavia was our exit to Europe, a region in which we had very good relations in the Balkans. It was our way out towards our possible expansion in the Third World," said Bulan Erdjevic. And Muntas Ozal, another case in point, the Foreign Minister of Turkey, said, "We believe that the Germans made a mistake because the former Yugoslavia was a model for co-existence among different nations. Europe made a mistake, having destroyed that model, and now we can see what the result of that was." Elizabeth Copp, the former Minister in the Swiss government, and an expert in the field of federalism, says the following: "I never understood this. It was a mistake and it was the mistake of one man and one foreign policy, a foreign policy, a man which I respected, Hans Dietrich Genscher. The international community is responsible for having recognised those states without solving the minority question beforehand and without going about it in a coordinated way. This had to have had a tragic end, and this was a big mistake made by Germany and the rest." Kissinger says, in the Welt an Zontag on the 8th of September, 1996, a German paper: "The recognition of an independent Bosnian state in 1992 did not cause the birth of the country but led to a civil war." And we have heard here that it is I who caused that civil war. The Bosnian Muslims, in fact, that their extremist part and their leadership worked against the Muslims in fact, in view of the number of Muslim countries. It was their detriment because it was the purposes of the big powers, and especially America, and this was a screen for their different behaviour towards Muslims and Muslim countries generally with respect to the way in which the big powers conducted themselves. The leaders of the Bosnian Muslims objectively played out their interests because the Bosnian Muslims lived in peace with the Serbs. They lived a normal life. And with the kind of policy they were waging, they did en masse and deliberately proclaim them to be casualties. They betrayed them. And so -- and there were a large number of Muslims in the Serbian army. They didn't join the army to kill the Muslims, I'm quite sure, but to defend themselves from a common evil, which was Islamic extremism which was seen to be a powerful weapon to destabilise the region and, in future, more and more the European continent as a whole. I have a very good illustration here, a document, which in very concrete, specific terms, and clearly, testifies to how this Islamic fundamentalist policy on the part of Izetbegovic and his party was opposed to any kind of peace at all which would have emerged in the tripartite peace negotiations at the Conference on Yugoslavia under the leadership of Vance and Owen and then Owen-Stoltenberg later on. This is a letter from the head office of Izetbegovic's party. It is signed by the secretary, Hasan Cengic, on their memorandum and paper with a stamp and seal. The 20th of the January, 1993 is the date. And it was addressed to the Party of Democratic Action, that is to say their leadership, in Trebinje in the territory of Republika Srpska. And the subject, it says: "Instruction about the moving out of Trebinje." And then it says: "As the situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina is becoming from one moment to the next with regard to security and safety more complicated, especially after the acceptance of the Geneva documents by Karadzic and his clique in Pale, it is necessary in order to have the aspirations of all Muslims fulfilled, that our country, Bosnia-Herzegovina, be strengthened and the following measures are to be undertaken in the terrain of the Trebinje municipality. First, via our activists who animate all Muslims, especially the prominent ones and the wealthier ones, to leave Trebinje as soon as possible and to move to Montenegro. Secondly, their property, mobile and immobile, partially to sell, et cetera, et cetera. And third, to exercise pressure and force against Muslims who do not act in conformity with this order and instructions. There is more but I have to save time. It says, with respect - "Selim Alikum" - the Secretary of the SDA, Hasan Cengic. I will tender this document so you can see it. And it is on the basis of this that this Municipal Board of the SDA, working in Republika Srpska in Trebinje, freely issues its own invitation in which it states the following: "The Serbo-Chetnik armada, together with his leader Karadzic, is trying to prevent us in our holy intentions and then our tricking the public at large in Geneva and shows falsely the loyalty of the Trebinje Muslims to the Serbo-Chetnik dictatorship and their loyalty to Republika Srpska and their military clique." And then he goes on to ask everybody to move out of the area. And as a minimum, the minimum we're asked for is that all Muslims should leave the so-called army of Republika Srpska forthwith and that it is our duty in sharing the fate of our entire people, a nation together with their families and our families and the rest of the citizens, that we should leave for Montenegro, et cetera. It goes on along those lines. Does this remind you of the same practice in Kosovo? Whether it does or not, all I can say is that I believe that the general public must associate this with what happened there straight away. So how can somebody serve in an army which is engaged in genocide against his own people? I don't say that this doesn't -- that this means that there were no war crimes. There were, of course. War crimes existed on all three sides. But this does mean that it was not the policy nor was an atmosphere of that kind created, nor did that kind of atmosphere exist in a broad sense. The victims and casualties of war against Yugoslavia were the innocent people from all three nations, all three ethnic groups. They were pushed into these conflicts and clashes because of foreign interests, other people's interests, but along with the full cooperation of their mindless leaders who led them to their death. In Croatia and in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the war was imposed. In Croatia, it was with confidence that they placed themselves under the protection of the United Nations and a political solution, because what they were promised was that they would be protected and that the problem would be resolved through political means. Up until the arrival of the United Nations, they were defending themselves. This was necessary defence. But from that time on, no military activities were undertaken on their part. I have here the notes from the 31st of December, that is to say the New Year between 1991 and 1992. Cyrus Vance came to see me, and he got my full support to send the blue helmets into Croatia and along the borders between Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina. And that in fact at the same time represented an indirect recognition by the international community of the direct involvement of Croatia in the events and occurrences in Bosnia-Herzegovina. And we gave not only verbal support when he came to visit me but also did so officially by an official stand on the part of the government. And when in Geneva from the 10th to the 13th of January, 1992, it was already quite clear that the plan would be adopted, the Muslim forces, on the 16th of January, no less, attacked the Serb municipality of Bratunac and launched a general offensive and perpetrated the massacre over the Serb population there. Otherwise, in the environs of Bratunac, 70 Serb villages were set fire to and the population slaughtered. Perhaps this map is a best illustration of how the problem is approached. It is Mr. Nice's map, and it shows Croatia and where the territories were, the territories which the Serbs had allegedly lived on and had allegedly seized. But what this map does not show, he didn't think of showing that it is precisely those territories which were the UN protected zones, and that I assume that the United Nations Security Council, at the proposal of the Special Envoy Cyrus Vance, did not make a decision to establish these protected zones until a political solution had been arrived because the Serbs had seized some sort of territory from the Croatian state but because a political solution had to be found. That's why it was done. And they all expected a political solution. Carrington spoke of this, and I quoted him a moment ago. He said that it was imminent. Now, as far as the Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina are concerned, they accepted the plan to hold a peace conference in Yugoslavia according to the Cutilheiro plan, as it was called. That happened before the clashes and conflict broke out. It was my stand and the official position of Serbia itself that any agreement which is reached by the three constituent peoples we would be happy to accept. And in visiting Turkey, I spoke about this. I had separate visits with the president of the republic, Mr. Ozal and the Prime Minister, Mr. Demirel, because I considered that it was not up to us to meddle in those affairs. They undertook the negotiations, they found their own solutions. The only thing we did consider was, and this proved to be correct, that the essence was in a solution which would guarantee the interests equally of each of the three constituent ethnic groups. And in my talks with Vance on the 4th of March -- this was publicised in the press and was clearly -- I clearly said to him that a political solution based on a consensus of three equal constituent nations can only represent a basis for defining the status of that republic. And I came out in favour of, on that occasion and that's what they wrote about, for a conference on Bosnia-Herzegovina to discuss the issue. And finally, this was the fifth round, the plan was signed. It was popularly known as Cutilheiro's plan. I'm not going to dwell on that particular plan now because my time is limited. But I do wish to stress that the vital element in that particular plan was the transformation of Bosnia from an unitary into a complex state form made up of three constituent entities which would prevent any majorisation or domination by any individual national group or ethnic group or two groups over a third group, et cetera. So the Serbs did accept this plan. They did accept an independent, autonomous Bosnia precisely with this element of equality; that all three ethnic groups should be equal within the state. There's a statement of Radovan Karadzic. It was carried after the signing of that agreement, and he says: "Every one of us lost any possibility of domination and got the possibility of not becoming a national minority." So what kind of Greater Serbian ambitions can anybody speak of here? It is interesting, actually. At that very same point in time, the spokesperson of Izetbegovic's SDA party, because Izetbegovic is one of the signatories of the Cutilheiro plan, confirmed -- and the spokesperson's name is Irfan Ajanovic, and I quote: "Confirmed that the SDA is pleased with this last agreement concerning Bosnia." And as for the possibility of the Serb Assembly to reject the Cutilheiro agreement, Ajanovic stated that that would have been an insane thing that would come from the Serb laboratory. And I quote him. "In that case, it's going to be quite clear as to who is deceiving the international community and the chairman of the Conference of Bosnia." End of quotation. Of course, at that time, little did he know that this insane thing would come out of the Muslim laboratory and that the Serb party -- that the Serb side would show maturity, political maturity, and wisdom. Very soon after the signing, Izetbegovic faithlessly withdrew his signature, and we saw that in the testimony on the tape. He did that after talking to Warren Zimmermann, the US Ambassador in Belgrade, and he was talked into it by Zimmermann. So this plan of salvation went down the drain before there was any conflict between them and a civil war began. Cutilheiro himself, surprised by Izetbegovic's decision, said on that occasion, "They obviously decided on a war option, and therefore, they have a great responsibility to assume." Regrettably, the warlords, and we see this here today, ascribe responsibility to the Serbs and to me personally, of course. So the absurdity is complete. After the renewed attempt made towards the end of 1992, I have a note on a meeting with Vance on Owen on the 6th of January, 1993, in Belgrade. My statement is there. I'm convinced that there is no way out of the crisis without respecting the equality of rights of all three peoples in Bosnia-Herzegovina and therefore I believe that the only way out is an immediate cessation of hostilities. And after that, negotiations about the principles that are a basis for respecting the rights of all three peoples. That is the only which in which long-lasting peace can be established. It is our duty to support all peaceful solutions that can lead to peace in this area. That support was confirmed in Geneva as well. And we saw from many elements, and also from the statement made by Owen, and I quoted it, that Izetbegovic rejected the Vance-Owen Plan because of the American position with regard to the plan, and that is why Owen asked the Americans and Clinton to exercise pressure on Izetbegovic. And even Kinkel on the 4th of February, asked the President of the United States to render his support in this peace plan, cautioning against the negative effects if this peace plan were not to be adopted. However, this support did not come, and it can be seen from the document I quoted a few minutes ago that it never crossed their minds to do anything else but to have a unitary Bosnia-Herzegovina conceived as a fundamentalist state. And it is not only that the Islamic declaration says what it's supposed to be. So in the war against Yugoslavia, the ethnic heterogeneity of Yugoslavia was abused. And in Bosnia, which everybody called a small-scale Yugoslavia, it could always have been abused. I can say that from the Berlin Congress in 1878 until the bombing of the Serb positions by NATO in 1995, foreign interference in Bosnian religious and ethnic conflicts always assumed the proportions of a humanitarian intervention. Foreign troops always came to Bosnia under the guise of doing good to the indigenous population. And it was always imperialist objectives and global strategies that were in the play, really. So if what was really wished for was to prevent ethnic and religious conflicts in Bosnia, what had to be upheld all the time was this sensitive ethnic balance and the equality of rights of all three peoples. Equality of rights means that all of the three Bosnian Herzegovinian nations' peoples should have the status of a constituent people that can exercise their sovereign rights and their own interests within the state entity of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Even according to Izetbegovic's words in Brussels and later according to Cutilheiro's plan, this plan did include certain political autonomies of every one of the political entities within Bosnia-Herzegovina. And conversely, statehood and full autonomy do not allow for any people in Bosnia-Herzegovina to be reduced to the status of a national minority. The best proof of this is the Dayton Accords themselves. There could have been no peace when this balance was disturbed. And when outvoting was encouraged. However, peace was achieved in Dayton through the recognition anew of the right of each and every three peoples to form this joint state and entities within Bosnia-Herzegovina. That was the necessary prerequisite and yet sufficient prerequisite without which this agreement could not have been brought to a successful end. However, it's not only Izetbegovic who was fickle. Obviously, it was the European Community too. Because precisely here in The Hague, at the Peace Palace on the 7th of September, 1991, there was a ceremonial inauguration of the Conference on the former Yugoslavia, and this was pursued by the European Community, and there was a declaration that includes the categorical statement that the community, I quote, "Will never recognise changes of borders that were not established by way of peaceful solutions." I don't have time to quote the positions we held then because time does fly. However, all of them say, and I said personally, many things. And there is the position of Serbia, there is the position of Yugoslavia, and all of this speaks in favour of advocating the equal treatment of all three peoples. I have here all these statements. There will be time for us to bring them to the fore. We supported five plans. And the European Ministerial Conference, at that conference, the last sentence I said: "Gentlemen, the very moment you take an equal attitude [in English] to all actors in the Yugoslav drama, you will take the decision on peace." [Interpretation] That was the position of Serbia. That was my position. That was the position that, in my opinion - and that is what I think today as well - was the only one that was principled in this entire affair. So it was not disintegration that was going on in Yugoslavia. This was unlawful secession, violent secession that gave rise to the first crimes that were committed in spite of the inviolability of borders and other principles enshrined in the UN Charter and the final act of Helsinki. So in fact, the alliance of external and internal protagonists actually opted for secession as the form of liquidating Yugoslavia. Actually, in this alliance, the right of peoples to self-determination, it was said, it did not pertain to peoples but to territories, as if the administrative borders, contrary to international and domestic law, were borders of sovereign states. And then they linked the right to self-determination to people after all, then yet again this did not apply to the Serb people. Yugoslavia as a state came into being through the union and free will of its own constituent peoples. Even the coat of arms of Yugoslavia, until the late 1960s, consisted of five flames that symbolised the five peoples; the Serbs, Croats, Slovenians, Macedonians and Montenegrins. And then, when the Muslims got the status of a constituent people, then in the late 1960s, a sixth flame was included in the coat of arms of Yugoslavia. So that became part of the coat of arms 20 years after the new Yugoslavia was established, in order to symbolise the sixth constituent people that were proclaimed then. This was actually the Muslim ethnic community. This German success in the campaign of recognition for the independence of Slovenia and Croatia, not to refer to newspaper articles now, however, Lord Carrington, in his letter to van den Brug, who was chairman at that time because the Netherlands was then presiding the European Community, they called it the bell that tolled for the country, and also he said that this was a spark that could set Bosnia and Herzegovina on fire. External political intervention selectively favoured the right to self-determination. In the case of Yugoslavia, the states of the European Community stimulated an anti-European concept of the establishment and creation of states, and they stimulated trampling upon norms of international and domestic law. The French President, Francois Mitterrand, in his statement on television on the 3rd of September in 1992, said that the international community bears part of the responsibility for the conflicts in Yugoslavia. He expressed his regrets that Europe, in the case of Yugoslavia, did not want to defend existing legal norms, and so on and so forth. It was clear to him that force was used, not the law, and that is why he expressed that regret. Unfortunately, too late. In the meantime, the world public opinion already at the very outset of the Yugoslavia crisis had certain prejudices imposed upon them. Geopolitical ones, cultural ones, civilisational differences between the East and West, and that this border was somewhere between Serbia and Croatia. Nobody abided by the norms of international law. Just like Hitler. In the 1930s, his platform was, Who pays any attention to the treaty of Versailles now? This is just a piece of paper from some French castle. We saw, 50 years later, precisely by a move made from that very same centre, the spectre of fascism and of the Ustasha idea emerged again. And also, half a century later, the independent State of Croatia as a fascist creation and the free and independent Republic of Croatia was created with the assistance of the Vatican factor, the German factor, and with the maximum assistance of emigres, Croatian emigres. Nobody concealed this; you saw it in that film, Croatia paid them back. That song, "Danke Deutschland," and in the island of Brac, they erected a monument to Hans Dietrich Genscher, still alive, and he was then Foreign Minister of Germany. The Vatican themselves made their role quite clear. Therefore, this so-called indictment for the war in Croatia and Bosnia is just as bad as the one for Kosovo, the previous one. The reason is quite simple: You do not have the truth in your hands, and you have to invent things, manipulate things, present half-truths, bring forth false witnesses. However, at this point in time, one thing does not seem clear, and that is that the actual truth is being unravelled and that the truth is coming to the fore regardless of historical forgeries - and I have given examples of that - and regardless of claims that are based precisely on these interests rather than on the actual state of affairs. In spite of unequivocal arguments that I have presented and that you should be aware of too if you believe that you are discharging your duties conscientiously, you accepted such accusations as it says here. It says: "Slobodan Milosevic took part in the joint criminal enterprise as mentioned in paragraphs," et cetera, et cetera. "The aim was to forcibly expel the Croat and other non-Serb population from one-third of the territory of the Republic of Croatia, a territory for which he planned to become part of a new state under Serb domination," and so on and so forth. In spite of all these facts and during those years, as a matter of fact before these crimes were committed, in the presence of the United Nations, we encouraged the normalisation of relations between Knin and Zagreb, and we thought that through this normalisation the way would be paved for a political solution. For example, on the 30th of November, 1994, the government of the Republic of Srpska Krajina, at its meeting in Knin, adopted the package of agreements with the Republic of Croatia, and according to the Prime Minister, once again unequivocally showed that they were in favour of a policy of peace and cooperation with the international community. And then again, on the 11th of January, 1995, at the UNPROFOR base at the Zagreb airport, Pleso [phoen], again a new round started, a round of talks between the delegations of the Republic of Croatia and the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Republic of Serbia Krajina concerning various measures. Talks are being held behind closed doors and Lord Owen and Thorwald Stoltenberg are present as well. Borislav Mikolic [phoen] heads the Krajina negotiating team and the head of the Croatian delegation is Hrvoj Saranic [phoen]. The same month, on the 24th in 1995, Stoltenberg comes to see me, and together we state that, through the efforts of the Contact Group, the peace process will be accelerated, and we supported this normalisation of relations between Knin and Zagreb, and so on. It is not possible to refer to all these elements, but there is no doubt that what was stated here is untrue and a total forgery.
